newsitem.title: USA: Campbell posts record results, splits stock.
newsitem.headline: Campbell posts record results, splits stock.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co. said Wednesday it had record second-quarter results as the company's soups, Pepperidge Farm cookies and Godiva chocolates enjoyed growing sales.
Campbell, celebrating the 100th anniversary of its world-famous soups, also announced a two-for-one stock split, payable to stockholders of record as of Feb. 24.
Net earnings rose 5 percent to $276 million, or $1.18 a share, in the quarter ended Jan. 26 from $257 million, or $1.03 a share, in the year-ago period.
Sales grew to $2.3 billion from $2.2 billion as volume sales of wet soup worldwide increased 7 percent.
U.S. sales for the quarter edged up 1 percent to $1.38 billion from $1.36 billion last year, driven by 9 percent growth in wet soup sales and 4 percent growth in wet soup volume.

"Our decision to split the stock comes at a time of strong investor confidence in Campbell's performance and reaffirms our commitment to building shareowner wealth," said David Johnson, Campbell chairman, president and chief executive.
Campbell, based in Camden, N.J., last split its stock on Dec. 2, 1991, on a two-for-one basis.

The company said its Red & White condensed soup, led by household favourites Chicken Noodle, Tomato and Cream of Mushroom, continued its strong volume growth. Campbell said its new 98 percent fat-free cream soups are proving to be one of the most successful new products in the condensed category.
Volume rose sharply for "V-8" vegetable juice with its new plastic container and "Franco-American" pasta featuring new "Superiore" for the adult market, it said.
Campbell's Food Service division continued its growth behind such strong products as new frozen Campbell's Restaurant Soups, "Prego" lasagna TV dinners and "Pace" Mexican sauces.

Bakery & Confectionery division sales, led by Pepperidge Farm and Godiva, rose 5 percent to $490 million from $466 million in the 1995 second quarter. Earnings rose by 10 percent to $73 million from $67 million, it said.

Campbell's said International Grocery sales rose 13 percent from a year ago to $470 million, due mainly to the acquisition in September of Erasco, Germany's leading soup company. But earnings were unchanged at $42 million after the division invested in consumer marketing in Asia, Canada and Japan and as speciality distribution companies in Europe fared poorly, it said.
Campbell's stock rose 62.5 cents to $85 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
